full_judgment:
K. M. Subhan, J.:- A petition under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition of Tenancy Act was filed by the pre-emptor-Respondents against the pre-emptee petitioner. The petition was dismissed by the Trial Court, but was allowed by the first appellate Court. The petitioners challenged the said order which was not entertained by the learned single judge of the then High Court, holding that the first appellate Court’s finding that the transferred land was an agricultural land and as such is subject to pre-emption, on an application under section 96 of the said Act was correct. 

 There is no force in this contention, because the finding that the transferred land is agricultural is on the basis of khatian and evidence and as such it is concluded by this finding of fact. Furthermore existence of non-agricultural land within the agricultural tenancy, does not affect the character of the land.
